item.title: Python File Pointer Position After Reading: Resetting Stream Position
item.description:
“Python File Pointer Position After Reading: Resetting Stream Position”

When working with file input/output in Python, developers frequently encounter a situation where a file object, after being fully read once, yields no further data upon subsequent attempts to read it using the same object. Why does this happen, and what are the reliable techniques to reposition the file stream to allow for re-reading the content?

This behavior stems from how file objects manage the reading process using an internal file pointer or cursor. When you iterate over a file or use methods like read() or readlines(), this pointer advances to the end of the file (EOF). Once at the EOF, subsequent read operations inherently find nothing left to consume.
